name: Mailtric
author: Abd Ur Rehman

sections.description:
Mailtric is a free WordPress email log and analytics plugin for reliable email delivery. It automatically records every email sent via wp_mail(), provides insights from logs, a one‑click resend tool, and an SMTP test to verify configuration. Use Mailtric to audit, debug, and improve the reliability of WordPress emails from WooCommerce, contact forms, membership sites, and more.

All features are included in the free plugin: full email logging, delivery analytics, one‑click resend, SMTP options, deliverability checks, database cleanup tools, and more. There is no pro version, no feature locking, and no usage limits – just install and start tracking your WordPress emails.

The interface is designed to feel native in WordPress and includes both light and dark mode layouts. Clear filters, search, and detail views make it easy to find any email and understand its delivery status.

Instead of guessing whether password resets, order confirmations, or contact form messages were delivered, you get a searchable, filterable email log and an at-a-glance dashboard of key email stats. This makes Mailtric ideal for:

  • Client sites where email reliability really matters.
  • WooCommerce and other e-commerce stores.
  • Membership, LMS, community, and booking sites.
  • Any WordPress site that can’t afford to lose important emails.

Mailtric focuses on logging, auditing and insights and works alongside your existing SMTP or transactional email service. You can use Mailtric’s optional SMTP settings or keep your current SMTP plugin — Mailtric enhances visibility with detailed logs and metrics either way.

Who Should Use Mailtric?

  • Store and review logs for WooCommerce order emails and other transactional messages.
  • Audit core WordPress notifications such as password resets and new user sign‑ups.
  • Debug contact form emails across popular form plugins.
  • Improve visibility for membership, LMS, community, and booking sites.
  • Reduce guesswork with clear send outcomes and one‑click resend tools.

Features

  • Full WordPress email logging
    Automatically log every email sent through wp_mail(). See subject, recipient, headers, and status in a clean email log.

  • Email deliverability insights & metrics
    Understand send outcomes and failures from logs to identify deliverability issues early.

  • Resend emails in one click
    Resend failed or bounced emails directly from the log. Perfect for critical emails like order confirmations, account activations, and password resets.

  • Clear analytics dashboard
    See email performance over time with visual stats and summary cards.

  • Smart filters & search
    Find emails by subject, recipient, date range, or status to debug issues fast.

  • Light & dark mode UI
    A modern interface that supports both themes for comfortable email log reviews.

  • Built to work with your stack
    Logs via wp_mail() so it works with popular form plugins, WooCommerce, membership plugins, and SMTP/transactional providers.

  • Performance-friendly
    Efficient logging designed to avoid slowing down your site.

  • Simple UI for non-developers
    Readable, intuitive screens suitable for clients and non‑technical users.

  • Multilingual interface (English, Spanish, French)
    Admin interface supports multiple languages for global sites.

  • All features are free
    No paid add‑ons or feature locking — everything shown is available in the free plugin.

Tools & Settings Overview

Mailtric includes a comprehensive Email Tools suite to help you verify configuration, diagnose deliverability, and manage your email logs:

  • Email Test – send a test email to confirm your site can send mail; handy check before troubleshooting deliverability.
  • SMTP Test – verify SMTP connection and authentication. Configure host, port, username, password and encryption (TLS/SSL) and run a connection test.
  • Deliverability Check – analyze your domain’s email reputation and DNS health, including SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MX records and blacklist status.
  • Database Management – clean old logs, remove failed logs, and optimize database tables and indexes.
  • Export / Import – export logs as CSV/JSON/XML or import a backup file to restore logs.
  • System Info – view environment diagnostics (WordPress/PHP/MySQL versions, server details) and copy a status report for support.

In Settings, Mailtric offers rich configuration to tailor logging and email behavior:

Settings tabs and key options

  • General

    • Email Notifications – receive notifications about email failures.
    • Delete Data on Uninstall – remove Mailtric data and email logs when uninstalling.
    • Save All Settings – persist changes site-wide.

  • SMTP

    • Enable SMTP – send emails via a custom SMTP server.
    • SMTP Host, Port, Username, Password.
    • Encryption – TLS or SSL.
    • From Email and From Name – set global sender identity.
    • Test Connection – verify SMTP connectivity and credentials.

  • Headers

    • X-Mailer Header – include a Mailtric identifier in outgoing emails.
    • Enable Address Overrides – add Reply‑To, CC, BCC and custom headers to all outgoing emails.
    • Force From Email / Force From Name – enforce SMTP sender identity and prevent overrides by other plugins/themes.
    • Reply‑To, CC, BCC – comma/newline separated entry fields.
    • Custom Headers – one per line in the format Name: Value.

  • Logging

    • Enable Logging – turn logging on/off.
    • Log Successful Emails – record emails that were sent.
    • Log Failed Emails – record emails that failed to send.
    • Log All Email Content – store complete email content (increases storage usage).
    • Log Custom Headers – store header metadata and apply them on resend.

  • Data Retention

    • Enable Data Retention – automatically delete old email logs.
    • Clean By – choose retention mode (e.g., log count).
    • Keep Maximum Logs – limit stored logs (e.g., 10,000).

  • Security

    • Require Authentication – users must be logged in to view logs.
    • Allowed User Roles – select which roles can access logs (Administrator, Editor, Author, etc.).
    • Enable API Access – allow external API access to email logs (coming soon).

  • Performance

    • Batch Size – number of emails to process in each batch.
    • Rate Limit (emails/hour) – maximum send rate.
    • Enable Queue – queue emails for background processing.

  • Setup Wizard

    • Prefer a guided setup? You can rerun the onboarding wizard anytime from the Settings page.

These tools and settings aim to make auditing, sending, and maintaining your WordPress email reliable and transparent.

Support

If you have questions, feature requests, or need help debugging an issue, please use the support forum on WordPress.org or the contact options linked from the Mailtric website.
sections.installation:
1. Install via WordPress (recommended)

    1. In your WordPress dashboard, go to Plugins → Add New.
    2. Search for “Mailtric”.
    3. Click Install Now, then Activate.

  2. Manual installation

    1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/mailtric.
    2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.

Once activated, Mailtric will begin logging emails sent via wp_mail() automatically. You’ll find the Mailtric pages in your WordPress admin menu.
sections.faq:
What emails does Mailtric log?

Mailtric logs emails sent via the WordPress wp_mail() function. This typically includes:

  • Core WordPress notification emails.
  • Contact form emails from most popular form plugins.
  • Transactional emails from WooCommerce and other e-commerce plugins that use wp_mail().
  • Membership, LMS, booking, and other plugin emails that rely on WordPress’ native mail system.

If a plugin uses wp_mail(), it will usually appear in the Mailtric logs.

Does Mailtric improve email deliverability by itself?

Mailtric doesn’t send emails – it monitors them. It gives you visibility into send status, opens, clicks, and bounces so that you can identify problems and then fix them by configuring a proper SMTP or email delivery service.

For best results, use Mailtric alongside a dedicated SMTP/email provider (such as SendGrid, Mailgun, SES, etc.) and use the logs and metrics to verify that configuration.

Can I resend emails?

Yes. You can resend selected emails directly from the Mailtric email log. This is particularly useful if your SMTP or email provider had a temporary issue and you want to re-send important messages.

Will this slow down my site?

Mailtric is designed to be efficient. It focuses on lightweight logging and uses optimised queries so it can run alongside your existing plugins without noticeably affecting performance.

Does Mailtric replace my SMTP plugin?

Mailtric focuses on email logging and analytics, and it also includes SMTP settings in the plugin’s Settings → SMTP tab. You can configure Mailtric to send emails via popular SMTP/transactional providers (e.g., SendGrid, Mailgun, Amazon SES, etc.).

While Mailtric provides a convenient SMTP configuration, its core purpose is visibility and insights (logging, resend, metrics). If you already use a dedicated SMTP plugin or service, Mailtric will work alongside it and enhance your understanding of what’s being sent and delivered.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • Changed: Bumped minimum PHP requirement to 8.0 for improved performance, security, and future compatibility.
  • Improved: Email log date formatting for accurate and readable timestamps (including reliable “time ago” rendering).
  • Improved: Email source detection to better attribute messages to popular plugins (e.g., WooCommerce, contact forms) instead of defaulting to “Mailtric”.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
